transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-11-24 15:00 PST (42m)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood CSM), Aisha (NexaHealth CTO), Daniel (ML Eng), Renee (Security Lead), Tom (DevOps)

Auto Summary (auto): onboarding progress, access setup, env readiness, security docs requested

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um quick check in on the onboarding items from last week
00:12 Aisha: hey Maya, thanks. Overall we're making progress. Dev account looks good, Daniel got the API keys and ran some smoke calls.
00:26 Daniel: yeah, we ran a few sample transcripts, got responses, latency seemed reasonable but we didn't push large sequences yet.
00:40 Carlos: cool, do you mind sharing the run config you used? token length, model, concurrency?
00:48 Daniel: I used redwood-hosted gpt-redwood-13b, default batch 1, sample prompts ~512 tokens, concurrency 3. Not ideal bench but first pass.
00:59 Carlos: ok that helps. For the poc we want both 1k tokens and 10k token runs to measure KV cache behaviour and seq-length perf. We'll include both in the spreadsheet.
01:12 Maya: quick update from our side on access: we see a partial VPC peering request in our logs, looks like peering CR pending, Tom?
01:20 Tom: yeah, I created the peering request but hit a permissions problem, I think on their side they need to accept or route table entries. I'll follow up with infra.
01:30 Renee: On the security front, we need SOC2 summary, network diagram, and our KMS integration pattern. Are those available?
01:40 Maya: yes, we'll send SOC2 summary and a redwood network diagram today. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys with the private deployment and dedicated via KMS integrations, we'll outline options.
01:56 Aisha: would prefer not to move to private unless we have to; if hosted can meet our encryption and residency needs that would be faster. But cost and latency need to be in check.
02:09 Carlos: understood. We'll run hosted bench first and show cost/latency delta vs our dedicated profile. For dedicated, quantization and batching profiles typically drop cost substantially but require longer setup.
02:28 Daniel: can you clarify fallback behaviour if we hit capacity? We need guaranteed availability during our peak windows.
02:35 Samir: good question — Redwood routing supports priority tiers and automated fallback to compatible model variants; we can propose an SLA-backed plan for Dedicated. We'll include details in the follow-up doc.
02:49 Renee: also SSO / SAML and RBAC — we need org SSO to be enforced, audit logs shipped to our SIEM. Is that supported?
02:57 Maya: yes SSO + RBAC supported; audit logs can be exported via our logging exporter to S3 (or pushed to your SIEM). We'll send the audit log schema.
03:10 Tom: one more infra question: do you require long-lived instance peering or do you support short-lived tunnels?
03:18 Carlos: we support both peering and transient tunnels for on-prem, but peering is preferred for perf. We'll document recommended route table configs.
03:30 Aisha: timeline check: our goal is pilot-ready by early Dec, production decision mid-Dec. Any blockers?
03:38 Maya: main blockers are VPC peering acceptance and us finishing the latency/cost benchmarks. Also security confirmation on KMS/Retention.
03:47 Daniel: I can help run some higher concurrency tests if Carlos shares the scripts.
03:52 Carlos: I'll push a small test harness (bash + python) to the shared drive, should be there by end of day. It will have both short and long-sequence runners.
04:02 Renee: for compliance, our infosec needs encryption in transit + at rest and key rotation controls; if hosted can't use our KMS, that's a showstopper.
04:14 Maya: we hear that; we'll outline the customer-managed KMS option and the private deployment tradeoffs. Also we have a dedicated offering where KMS integration is straightforward.
04:26 Aisha: price sensitivity — can you give an estimate of delta between hosted and dedicated for our expected qps?
04:33 Carlos: rough numbers now: hosted unit price per token higher but no infra commit; dedicated with reserved capacity reduces unit cost by ~30-45% depending on quantization. We'll produce a model once we have your workload profile.
04:50 Daniel: small note — our prompt templates include many system-level instructions, so output size is big; we should test response-length trimming or rersampling to control cost.
05:01 Carlos: yes we can demo prefix caching and KV cache hits to reduce cost. We'll instrument the tests to show cache-hit rates.
05:17 Maya: ok, let's capture action items and owners. Samir, can you read them back?
05:22 Samir: sure. 1) Maya to send SOC2 and network diagram by Thu 11/26. 2) Carlos to run 1k & 10k token latency/cost benchmark and upload spreadsheet by 11/30. 3) Tom to complete VPC peering acceptance + provide test IAM by 11/27. 4) Renee to confirm KMS/retention requirements by 11/30. 5) Redwood to share audit log schema and SSO docs.
05:48 Renee: sounds good. Minor transcription note — earlier the demo had some stutter, probably our sandbox network. We'll see once peering is ready.
06:00 Aisha: thanks everyone. For next meeting, let's review the benchmark numbers and decide whether to proceed with a short canary on hosted or spin up dedicated infra.
06:12 Maya: agreed. We'll aim for a canary week of Dec 7; if bench looks good we'll do hosted canary, otherwise start dedicated provisioning.
06:23 Tom: I'll prioritize the peering. I'll ping infra and share the acceptance screenshot.
06:30 Maya: perfect thanks all. Meeting close.

Notes: transcript has occasional mislabels and auto-generated sections; customer references to product names sometimes approximate (e.g., gpt-redwood-13b typed as redwood-13b).

End of transcript.
